title: Async Streaming Pipeline with Backpressure & Batching
problemStatement: Implement `async function* batchAsyncStream(asyncIterable, batchSize)` that reads from an async iterable source and yields arrays of items chunked by `batchSize`. Any remaining items when the stream closes must be yielded in a final partial batch.
interviewTrap: Failing to handle trailing remaining items when an async iterator completes causes silent data loss. Consuming without backpressure risks memory ballooning.

testCases.name: Chunks stream into equal batches
testCases.testFn: async function* src() { yield 1; yield 2; yield 3; yield 4; } const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

testCases.name: Flushes remaining items on stream completion
testCases.testFn: async function* src() { yield 1; yield 2; yield 3; yield 4; yield 5; } const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

testCases.name: Yields nothing for empty stream
testCases.testFn: async function* src() {} const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

details.name: Flushes remaining items on stream completion

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Generators are re-entrant state machines. When yield is encountered, the generator's execution context is suspended and pushed out of the call stack. Calling .next() re-attaches the context and resumes evaluation.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Async Generators & Flow Control Backpressure.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Async Generators & Flow Control Backpressure is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
